key_insight: CARM prevents positive and negative token-level probability changes from canceling out, making response-level off-policy masking more sensitive and reliable for LLM RL.
engineering_relevance: It gives practitioners a theoretically grounded way to filter rollout responses during RL post-training, which can improve stability and quality in reasoning and code models.
method: Compute token log-ratios between sampled rollout and training policies.
Take the absolute value of each token log-ratio before averaging at the sequence level.
Accept responses only when the masked statistic satisfies a joint bound on out-of-band ratio frequency and mean log-distance.
evidence_signal: On math reasoning and code generation benchmarks, CARM improved mean@16 by up to 3.13 points over geometric-mean masking and raised average pass@1 by 2.88 points over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Absolute-value masking may be more conservative and depends on careful thresholding to avoid rejecting useful but shifted responses.
paper_title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning
